mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which stimulates economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects stronger consumer demand, which positively impacts the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite rising HOUST values, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 consistently shows positive returns when UNRATE increases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals stronger supply chains, positively affecting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL), real economic growth is positive, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth does not outpace CPIAUCSL and S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% indicates tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% and S&P 500 returns remain positive, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, increasing real consumer spending (RSAFS) signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns in late-cycle phases, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases and unemployment (UNRATE) decreases, labor market strength boosts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS and UNRATE move inversely and S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is rejected.
